slot.brief: Use bond enthalpies of reactants and products to compute ΔH of a combustion/formation reaction via Hess-type addition.

stem: For the combustion of propane, $\text{C}_3\text{H}_8(g)+5\text{O}_2(g)\rightarrow3\text{CO}_2(g)+4\text{H}_2\text{O}(g)$. Given mean bond enthalpies in kJ mol$^{-1}$: C–C $=347$, C–H $=413$, O=O $=498$, C=O in $\text{CO}_2=799$, and O–H $=463$, the enthalpy change per mole of propane is
working:
$$\Delta H=\sum E(\text{bonds broken})-\sum E(\text{bonds formed})$$
$$=[2(347)+8(413)+5(498)]-[6(799)+8(463)]$$
$$=6488-8498=-2010\ \text{kJ mol}^{-1}$$

Independent check: Bonds broken: 2(347) + 8(413) + 5(498) = 6488 kJ mol⁻¹. Bonds formed: 6(799) + 8(463) = 8498 kJ mol⁻¹. ΔH = 6488 − 8498 = −2010 kJ mol⁻¹.
